correctness.rationale: The radial normalization b_n=(cn)^(-1/alpha) makes n P(1-rho<=b_n s) tend to s^alpha, with independent uniform directions, giving the stated locally finite Poisson law. A regular-simplex cap configuration gives a uniform negative direction for any candidate center shift. This both bounds the finite center on scale b_n using R_n<=1 and makes the limiting envelope coercive. On each finite depth slab condition on the Poisson count, and use the unordered iid representation: no <=d normals balance zero, every d+1 lifted rows are independent, and a diffuse last depth prevents d+2 constraints from binding at one point. First-order optimality forces balance, so exactly d+1 active directions enclose zero in their interior. Their span rules out two maximizers by testing the midpoint; an a.s. unique minimal depth rules out Z=0, and equivariance gives the rotation-invariant law. The sign is +u·z: the first-order expansion of the distance subtracts b_n(s+u·z). In a coupling of the vague point measures all finite integer cutoffs match eventually, including some which supply shielding and make deeper observations irrelevant by the triangle bounds. Thus the objectives converge on compact sets containing their maximizers, and uniqueness gives joint center/radius convergence. Strict slack excludes all observations outside the limiting active group from the finite boundary, and the Euclidean enclosing-ball first-order condition excludes each proper subset of that group. This proves eventual full boundary count on the coupling, not just the existence of a support set. The repair makes the coupling and genericity explicit and separates established coverage in the uniform special case; the theorem itself is retained.
residual_risks: Requires fixed dimension and an actual one-term radial tail equivalence, not arbitrary two-sided power bounds.
Does not supply convergence rates or a closed-form center density; none is inferred from the finite diagnostics.
